ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute with no refund; no driver violation is recorded (traffic reason on the replaced stretch, F11) and no account flag applies (RD-6 not met, F17).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 10.9 km against an optimal 8.4 km, a deviation of 2.52 km billed / 2.31 km on the single off-route segment 12:19–12:25 [F1][F3][F4]. That is over the 1 km tolerance, so a route-deviation assessment is triggered [RD-1].

Before the segment began (12:19), the driver messaged at 12:15: "Jam ahead on Ayer Rajah Expressway, I'm going via Clementi Avenue 2." [F7]. The rider replied at 12:16: "hmm ok lor" [F8]. Read in context, that is an assent to the driver's stated route, sent before the segment started [F7][F8][F9][RD-5]. The driver's later written statement to the same effect is not itself consent and I give it no weight [F10][RD-5].

The words name a specific road, Clementi Avenue 2, so this is a named-road agreement rather than a general route choice [F7][F8][RD-5]. The segment's roads driven include CLEMENTI AVENUE 2 [F3], so the named road was tied to the segment and the agreement covers the whole segment — the roads before and after it are part of going via Clementi Avenue 2 [F3][F7][F8][RD-5]. The segment's 2.31 km is therefore exempt under RD-5.

There was also a traffic reason on the replaced stretch: Ayer Rajah Expressway at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) from 12:06 to 12:25, covering the segment window [F11][F3][RD-4]. That is why the trace records no driver violation; it does not exempt the segment, the consent above does that [RD-4][RD-2].

On the agreed exemption, 2.52 km − 2.31 km = 0.21 km remains, which is ≤ 1 km, so no amount is payable: 0.21 × $1.4100 = $0.30, below the 1 km tolerance, and no refund arises [F4][F1][F3][RD-1][RD-2]. Had the segment counted, the excess-distance fare would have been 2.52 km × $1.4100/km = $3.55, but it does not [F4][RD-2].

The 0.19–0.21 km difference between the billed excess and the segment's added km is within the deviation tolerance and there is nothing else off-route on the record, so the outcome is no refund [F1][F3][F4][RD-1][RD-2].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so no account flag is available even on an upheld deviation [F17][RD-6].

The figure $3.55 (2.52 km × $1.4100/km) is correct arithmetic [F4][RD-2], but the exempt segment leaves only 0.21 km, within the 1 km tolerance, so nothing is refundable [F3][RD-1][RD-2].
Withdrawn and not available: route disputes upheld in the last 90 days = 0, so RD-6's repeat criterion is unmet [F17][RD-6].
Accepted; the rider's profile is clean [F16], but profile facts never decide the case, and the outcome turns on the chat and GPS record [F7][F8][F3].

Accepted only in outcome: on the exemption of the segment [F3][F7][F8][RD-5], 2.52 km − 2.31 km = 0.21 km remains, ≤ 1 km, so no refund [F4][F1][RD-1][RD-2]; the double-counting objection on the figures is not material to this result.
Accepted as a reading of the record: nothing in the chat, the complaint or the statement raises safety, so no SAFE-1 escalation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1].
